background_notes.fact: For every natural r, r! is a positive natural integer, hence its images in Z and C are nonzero. Thus (r!:C)(r!:C)^(-1)=1, and multiplication by a product of factorials can be cancelled in Z or C.

grounds.reason: D003 defines X_r using the complex inverse of r! for natural r.
D004 defines Y_r with the same natural factorial denominator.

background_notes.justification: The empty factorial product is 1; every factor of any nonempty factorial is a positive integer. Their finite product is positive. The standard embeddings Z→C and N→Z preserve these nonzero integers, and cancellation follows in the integral domain Z and field C.

background_notes.justification: Every vector has a unique finite basis expansion sum_k a_k e_k. Set T(sum_k a_k e_k)=sum_k a_k w_k. Uniqueness of coordinates makes this well-defined; addition and scalar multiplication of coordinates prove complex linearity. The same expansion proves uniqueness.
